_meta.description: MoneyBTI 钱格 人格卡知识库 v4。22 张卡来自组员的《人格设计 1 / 2》：类别型 11 张用 mode=count（5 条条件满足 ≥ 3 条即命中；需历史账单的条件在单月数据上不计入分母），金额 / 时间 / 特别 / 兜底 11 张用 mode=any（任一规则组全部满足）。每条条件按分段线性打成 0–100 分（阈值 = 60 分），卡匹配度 = 条件分的加权平均（条件即维度）。special 卡 override=true 时命中即主人格；月底渡劫人 special 但不覆盖，作为并列人格。全勤 / 一日暴走 / 薅羊毛为成就徽章，不作人格。signature 字段是 v3 的 12 维原型，只用于评估对照 B'。
_meta.categories_note: C11 宠物 为 v4 新增类别
_meta.i18n: 字段 *_en 为英文版（名称取设计稿英文名，其余由 eval/translate_kb.py 翻译后人工抽查）；M6 / M7 按 lang 参数选用中文或英文字段。

cards.name: 外卖包月户

conditions.label: 外卖占餐饮支出 ≥ 50%
conditions.label_en: Delivery accounts for ≥ 50% of dining spend

conditions.label: 至少 3 周出现外卖
conditions.label_en: Delivery appears in at least 3 weeks

conditions.label: 外卖笔数明显高于生鲜（≥ 1.5 倍）
conditions.label_en: Delivery order count significantly higher than groceries (≥ 1.5x)

cards.tagline: 厨房可以不开火，外卖软件不能没会员。
cards.tagline_en: The kitchen can stay cold. Your delivery app can’t.
cards.interpretation: 你不是不会做饭，只是觉得人生已经够忙了，没必要再为“今天吃什么”多开一个副本。对你而言，外卖软件是第二食堂，骑手是最熟悉的陌生人，从工作日午餐到凌晨夜宵，总有一单正在路上。
cards.interpretation_en: It’s not that you can’t cook—life is just busy enough without the “What should I eat?” side quest. Delivery apps are your second kitchen, and your rider might be the most familiar stranger in your life. From weekday lunches to midnight cravings, there’s always something on the way.
cards.core_categories: 通过外卖平台、餐饮配送平台产生的正餐、快餐、早餐、夜宵等配送型餐饮消费。
cards.focus: 高频 + 持续 + 配送型餐饮 + 明显的外卖使用习惯

cards.tone: 轻松、有共鸣、不带消费羞辱
slogan_examples: The kitchen can stay cold. Your delivery app can’t.

cards.core_categories_en: Meals, fast food, breakfast, late-night snacks, and other delivery-based dining purchases made through delivery platforms or food delivery apps.
guardrails_en: Do not assume high-frequency online shopping indicates 'shopping addiction' or lack of self-control.
Do not describe frequent online shopping as 'wasteful' or 'reckless spending'.
Do not assume purchased items are unnecessary or have no practical use.
Do not infer user income, wealth, or financial status from purchase amounts.
Do not infer user gender, occupation, or social status from purchased items.
Do not label high-frequency small orders as 'impulsive shopping' unless supported by other clear behavioral data.
It's okay to playfully reference typical online shopping scenarios like cart, bundling, coupons, and delivery notifications, but keep it light, relatable, and non-shaming.
distinguish_en: When purchasing milk tea via delivery platforms, if the specific merchant can be identified as a tea brand, prioritize counting it under milk tea consumption traits.
cards.focus_en: High frequency + consistency + delivery-based dining + clear delivery usage habits

conditions.label: 至少 3 周出现茶饮
conditions.label_en: Tea drinks appear in at least 3 weeks

conditions.label: 同一茶饮商户复购 ≥ 3 次
conditions.label_en: Repeat purchase at same tea shop ≥ 3 times

conditions.label: 茶饮笔数明显高于零食甜品（≥ 1.5 倍）
conditions.label_en: Tea drink orders significantly higher than snacks/desserts (≥ 1.5x)

cards.tagline: 生活可以偶尔有点苦，手里的奶茶必须是甜的。
cards.tagline_en: Life can be bitter. Your milk tea doesn’t have to be.
cards.interpretation: 对你来说，奶茶不是一笔普通的支出，而是生活里的小型快乐补给站。你懂得用一杯喜欢的味道，给普通的一天加点仪式感：上课前来一杯、工作累了来一杯、朋友见面再来一杯。别人靠充电宝续航，你靠的是三分糖、少冰和加珍珠。
cards.interpretation_en: Milk tea isn’t just another expense—it’s your little happiness refill. Before class, after a long day, or when meeting friends, there’s always a good reason for a cup. Some people carry a power bank to stay charged. You? 30% sugar, less ice, extra pearls.
cards.core_categories: 奶茶、新式茶饮、果茶、鲜奶茶等现制茶饮消费。
cards.focus: 消费频次 > 持续性 > 重复购买 > 消费金额
distinguish: 奶茶续命体 ≠ 外卖包月户，如果通过外卖平台购买奶茶，以奶茶特征优先，遵“具体消费类别 > 消费渠道”，不因为用户喜欢叫奶茶外卖，就同时过度提高“外卖包月户”的得分。
cards.tone: 轻松、有共鸣、不带消费羞辱
slogan_examples: Life can be bitter. Your milk tea doesn’t have to be.
guardrails: 不根据奶茶消费频率判断用户存在“成瘾”
不根据茶饮账单推断用户的体重、健康状况或饮食问题
不评价用户喝奶茶“太多”“应该少喝”
不将高频小额茶饮消费描述为浪费
不默认用户购买奶茶是因为压力大、疲劳或情绪问题

可以使用“续命”“快乐 Buff”“续杯”等轻松网络表达
人格解读重点突出小额悦己、日常仪式感和高频茶饮习惯

cards.core_categories_en: Consumption of freshly made tea drinks: milk tea, new-style tea, fruit tea, fresh milk tea, etc.
guardrails_en: Do not judge users as 'addicted' based on milk tea purchase frequency
Do not infer users' weight, health status, or dietary issues from tea drink bills
Do not comment that users drink 'too much' milk tea or 'should drink less'
Do not describe frequent small-amount tea purchases as wasteful
Do not assume users buy milk tea due to stress, fatigue, or emotional issues
Do not infer users' income or economic level from the brands they buy
May use lighthearted internet expressions like 'life-saving', 'happiness buff', 'refill'
Personality interpretation should highlight small self-indulgence, daily rituals, and frequent tea-drinking habits
distinguish_en: Milk Tea Lifeline ≠ Takeout Monthly Subscriber: if users buy milk tea via delivery platforms, prioritize milk tea traits. Follow 'specific consumption category > consumption channel' — do not over-score 'Takeout Monthly Subscriber' just because users order milk tea delivery.
cards.focus_en: Purchase frequency > Consistency > Repeat purchases > Spending amount

cards.name: 探店雷达

conditions.label: 单一商户 ≤ 30% 的堂食笔数
非快餐连锁占线下餐饮 ≥ 40%

cards.tagline: 你的美食地图没有终点，只有下一个新坐标。
cards.tagline_en: Same city, new table.
cards.interpretation: 你的美食地图永远处于更新状态。比起反复光顾熟悉的老地方，你更容易被一家没吃过的新店勾起兴趣：新开的 Brunch、藏在巷子里的小馆、朋友刚推荐的餐厅，都可能成为你的下一站。对你来说，吃饭不只是解决一餐，更像是在城市里不断解锁新的坐标。好吃就加入收藏，偶尔踩雷也是体验——毕竟宝藏小店，都是一家一家试出来的。
cards.interpretation_en: Your food map is always getting new pins. A new café, a hidden restaurant, or a friend’s latest recommendation—you’re ready to try it. For you, eating out is more than just getting fed. It’s a tiny adventure around the city. Some become favorites, some become funny mistakes. That’s the deal—hidden gems don’t find themselves.
cards.core_categories: 线下餐厅、特色餐饮、咖啡馆、Brunch、甜品店、餐酒馆等具有一定体验属性的餐饮消费。
cards.focus: 商户多样性 + 新店率 + 持续探索行为
distinguish: 探店雷达 ≠ 外卖包月户，外卖包月户强调的是配送、高频和便利性；探店雷达强调的是线下、多商户和探索性。
探店雷达 ≠ 奶茶续命体，消费涉及多个品牌的奶茶、果茶等现制茶饮，应优先计入「奶茶续命体」的识别范围。
如果用户长期在同一家连锁咖啡店高频消费，不应该仅因为消费频繁就判断为探店；如果用户持续前往不同独立 Cafe、Brunch 店等，则可以增强「探店雷达」得分。
cards.tone: 轻松、有共鸣、不带消费羞辱
guardrails: 不将频繁尝试新餐厅描述为“跟风消费”
不默认用户探店是为了拍照、发社交媒体或追逐网红店
不因为线下餐饮支出较高而评价用户“浪费钱”或“不会过日子”
不根据餐厅档次或消费金额推断用户收入、财富或社会地位
不根据餐饮频率推断用户体重、健康状况或饮食问题
不默认“新店率高”意味着用户喜新厌旧
可以使用“踩雷”“宝藏店”“解锁新坐标”等轻松表达
人格解读重点突出探索欲、尝鲜倾向、商户多样性和体验导向
summary_examples: 你的美食地图没有终点，只有下一个新坐标。
你的美食地图永远处于更新状态。比起反复光顾熟悉的老地方，你更容易被一家没吃过的新店勾起兴趣：新开的 Brunch、藏在巷
cards.core_categories_en: Dine-in restaurants, specialty dining, cafés, brunch spots, dessert shops, bistro bars — any food & drink experience with a vibe.
guardrails_en: Don't label frequent new restaurant visits as 'trend-following'
Don't assume users dine out just for photos, social media, or hype spots
Don't judge users as 'wasting money' or 'can't manage life' based on higher dine-in spending
Don't infer income, wealth, or social status from restaurant tier or spending amount
Don't infer weight, health, or eating habits from dining frequency
Don't assume a high new-store rate means users are fickle
Light expressions like 'hit or miss', 'hidden gem', 'unlock a new spot' are fine
Focus interpretation on curiosity, novelty-seeking, merchant diversity, and experience orientation
distinguish_en: Restaurant Radar ≠ Delivery Devotee — Delivery Devotee is about convenience, frequency, and ordering in; Restaurant Radar is about dine-in, variety, and exploration.
Restaurant Radar ≠ Boba Lifeline — if consumption involves multiple brands of milk tea, fruit tea, or other made-to-order drinks, prioritize Boba Lifeline identification.

If a user frequently visits the same chain coffee shop, don't label them as a spot-hunter just because of high frequency; if they consistently visit different independent cafés, brunch spots, etc., that strengthens the Restaurant Radar score.
cards.focus_en: Merchant diversity + new-store rate + sustained exploration behavior

cards.name: 快递召唤师

conditions.label: 至少 3 周有网购
conditions.label_en: Online shopping in at least 3 weeks

cards.tagline: 世界那么大，你选择让它包邮到家。
cards.tagline_en: The world is huge. You prefer it delivered.
cards.interpretation: 你的购物车很少真正空过，生活里缺什么，第一反应就是上网搜一搜。日用品该补就补，喜欢的衣服先加购，偶尔刷到有意思的小玩意，也很容易顺手带回家。对你来说，网购早就不只是买东西，更像是一套熟练的生活补给系统：挑一挑、比比价、领个券，再等着包裹陆续上门。别人出门逛世界，你更擅长让世界打包好，自己送到门口。
cards.interpretation_en: Your shopping cart is rarely truly empty. Need something for daily life? Search it online. See an outfit you like? Add to cart. Find a random little thing that looks useful or fun? It might be coming home too. Online shopping has become your personal supply system: browse, compare, grab a deal, and wait for the packages to roll in. Some people go out to shop the world. You prefer having the world delivered to your door.

cards.focus: 网购频次和持续性 > 单纯网购金额

cards.name: 菜场理财家

conditions.label: 食材占餐饮支出 ≥ 30%
conditions.label_en: Groceries account for ≥ 30% of food & drink spending

conditions.label: 食材笔数明显高于外卖（≥ 1.5 倍）
conditions.label_en: Grocery trips clearly outnumber takeout orders (≥ 1.5x)

cards.tagline: 不是舍不得花，是每一块钱都要花得明白。
cards.tagline_en: Not cheap. Just making every dollar count.
cards.interpretation: 你的账单里藏着最真实的人间烟火：今天买菜，明天补水果，路过超市还不忘看看鸡蛋有没有打折。比起把三餐交给外卖，你更喜欢自己掌握生活的节奏。你知道什么值得囤货、什么现买更新鲜，也清楚什么值得买、怎么买更划算。对你来说，把日子过好不一定需要大手笔，会买、会挑、会安排，本身就是一种生活能力。
cards.interpretation_en: Your spending is full of everyday life: veggies today, fruit tomorrow, and maybe eggs if they’re on sale. Instead of leaving every meal to a delivery app, you like having a little more control over your daily routine. You know what’s worth stocking up on, what’s better fresh, and how to get the best value for your money. For you, living well doesn’t have to cost a lot—knowing what to buy, how to choose, and how to plan is a skill of its own.
cards.core_categories: 菜市场 / 生鲜超市 / 社区生鲜 / 水果店 / 肉禽蛋奶 / 粮油调味 / 线上生鲜平台等家庭食材类消费。
cards.focus: 购买频次 + 持续性 > 单次消费金额
distinguish: 菜场理财家 ≠ 外卖包月户
高频购买食材、外卖频率较低 → 「菜场理财家」特征更强高频点外卖、食材采购较少 → 「外卖包月户」特征更强
两者不必完全互斥。如果用户工作日经常点外卖、周末又规律买菜，可以分别计算钱格匹配度。
菜场理财家 ≠ 快递召唤师
即使通过线上平台购买蔬菜、水果、肉类、米面粮油等，也应该优先识别为食材消费，而不是普通网购
cards.tone: 轻松、有共鸣、不带消费羞辱
slogan_examples: Not cheap. Just making every dollar count.

不根据食材采购行为推断用户收入较低、经济困难或消费能力有限
不根据买菜频率推断用户的性别、婚姻状态或家庭角色
不默认高频购买食材意味着用户本人每天做饭
不将购买促销、折扣商品描述为“贪便宜”
不因为用户外卖消费较少，就评价其生活方式“更健康”或“更自律”
可以轻松调侃买菜、看价格、挑食材、囤货等场景，但应突出会规划、懂生活和消费有掌控感

你的账单里藏着最真实的人间烟火：今天买菜，明天补水果，路过超市还不忘看看鸡蛋有没有打折。比起把三餐交给外卖，你更喜欢自己
cards.core_categories_en: Wet markets / fresh supermarkets / community grocery stores / fruit shops / meat, poultry, eggs & dairy / grains, oils & condiments / online fresh food platforms — any household grocery spending.
guardrails_en: Don't describe price-checking, discounts, or value-seeking as 'stingy' or 'cheap'
Don't infer low income, financial hardship, or limited spending power from grocery buying behavior
Don't infer gender, marital status, or family role from grocery shopping frequency
Don't assume frequent grocery buyers cook every day themselves
Don't describe buying discounted or promotional items as 'being greedy for a bargain'
Don't judge a lifestyle as 'healthier' or 'more disciplined' just because takeout spending is low
Feel free to playfully reference scenes like grocery shopping, price-checking, picking produce, or stocking up — but highlight planning skills, life savvy, and a sense of control over spending
distinguish_en: Market Money Manager ≠ Takeout Monthly Pass Holder
Frequent grocery buying, low takeout frequency → stronger 'Market Money Manager' traits. Frequent takeout, little grocery buying → stronger 'Takeout Monthly Pass Holder' traits.
The two aren't mutually exclusive. If a user orders takeout often on weekdays but regularly buys groceries on weekends, calculate Money Personality match separately.
Market Money Manager ≠ Delivery Summoner
Even if groceries (vegetables, fruit, meat, rice, oil, etc.) are bought through online platforms, they should still be identified as grocery spending, not general online shopping.
cards.focus_en: Purchase frequency + consistency > single transaction amount

cards.name: 精致主义者

conditions.label: 品质 / 形象类消费 ≥ 6 次
美发 / 美甲 / 美容服务 ≥ 2 次

cards.tagline: 钱可以少花，但生活不能将就。
cards.tagline_en: Spend less? Maybe. Settle for less? Never.
cards.interpretation: 你愿意为生活里的“质感”买单。护肤、美妆、穿搭、香水，或是那些让日常变得更精致舒适的小物，都可能出现在你的账单里。你不一定追求最贵，但会在意品质、设计和体验感。对你来说，精致不是把生活堆满昂贵的东西，而是在能力范围内认真选择自己喜欢的生活方式。该省的可以省，该讲究的绝不将就。
cards.interpretation_en: You're willing to pay for 'texture' in life. Skincare, makeup, fashion, perfume, or those little things that make everyday life more refined and comfortable — they might all show up on your bill. You don't necessarily go for the priciest, but you care about quality, design, and experience. For you, being refined isn't about filling life with expensive stuff — it's about thoughtfully choosing the lifestyle you love within your means. You can save where it counts, but you never settle when it matters.

cards.interpretation: 你的消费单位可能和别人不太一样，你买东西大概率不看右下角。别人纠结的是“要不要买”，你考虑的是“买几个”。价格标签对你来说跟一张纸没区别。从吃饭到购物，预算参考是“我乐意”。偶尔买一次贵的不算什么，大家都有奢侈消费，但你的账单里一笔接一笔都保持着这个水准，那只能说：银行卡的颜色可以很多，但你手里只有黑色的。

Coffee in the morning, a snack after lunch, a quick convenience-store stop, then a ride home at night. Every purchase looks harmless. cards.tagline_en: STARTED WITH “SWIPE.”， ENDED WITH “I’M FINE.”
cards.interpretation: 你的一个月像是被硬生生切成了两个经济周期。月初的你相信钱是流动的，喜欢就买、想吃就点，银行卡最大的作用就是证明“支付成功”；到了月底，消费欲望突然开始讲道理，外卖变成“家里其实还有吃的”，购物车变成“下个月再说”，连路过便利店都多了一份定力。不是月底的你突然成熟了，只是月初的你多少有点没给月底的自己留活路。好消息是：距离下个月月初，已经不远了。
cards.interpretation_en: Your month seems to run on two completely different economies. At the beginning, money is meant to move—see it, want it, swipe it. Your card’s main job is basically to say “Payment Successful.” Then the end of the month arrives, and suddenly you become financially enlightened. Delivery becomes “There’s food at home.” Your shopping cart becomes“Maybe next month.” Even the convenience store can no longer tempt you. It’s not that end-of-month you suddenly became responsible. Beginning-of-month you just left them very little choice. Good news: next month is almost here.

cards.interpretation: 你的账单里不只有消费，还有一张看不见的社交关系网。今天帮朋友垫一下饭钱，明天收一笔 AA，生日发个红包，聚会结束再负责把账算明白，钱在你的账户里进进出出，总能和某个人联系起来。对你来说，转账不只是数字从一个账户跑到另一个账户，也是朋友之间一句“我先来”“一会儿转你”。如果朋友圈需要一个结算中心，你大概已经在没有工资的情况下上岗很久了。
cards.interpretation_en: Your transaction history isn’t just about spending—it’s also a map of your social life. You cover dinner today, collect someone’s share tomorrow, send a birthday red packet, and somehow end up settling the bill after every group outing. Money moves in and out of your account, but there’s usually a friend attached to it. If your group chat ever needed a finance department, congratulations: you’ve probably been running it for free.

cards.tagline: 弱水三千，只刷一家。
cards.tagline_en: ONE STORE. ONE HEART.
cards.interpretation: 世界上店那么多，你的钱包偏偏只对一家长情。第一次消费可能是偶遇，第二次算回购，等到同一个名字在账单里出现二三十次，这段关系显然已经不能用“经常去”简单概括。别人货比三家，你负责认准一家；新品可以看，新店可以路过，但最后付款的时候还是熟悉的那个名字。弱水三千，只刷一家——这不是重复消费，这是 commitment。
cards.interpretation_en: There are countless stores out there, yet your wallet keeps choosing the same one. The first purchase might be a coincidence, the second a repeat, but once the same merchant appears twenty or thirty times, “regular customer” starts to feel like an understatement. Others shop around; you stay committed. New stores may come and go, but when it’s time to pay, somehow it’s always the same name. This isn’t repetition—it’s a relationship.
cards.core_categories: 同一咖啡店 / 奶茶店 / 餐厅 / 便利店 / 超市 / 品牌门店 / 电商店铺等产生的高频重复消费；排除因外卖平台统一显示商户名称而造成的误判

cards.name: 端水大师
cards.tagline: 什么都花一点，什么都不上头。
cards.tagline_en: BALANCED. MOSTLY.A LITTLE OF EVERYTHING.
cards.interpretation: 想从你的账单里挑一个最突出的爱好并不容易，因为每个类别都被你照顾得相当周到。吃饭要有，购物不能少，交通、娱乐和日常生活也一个没落下，谁都分到一点，但谁也别想独占钱包。别人消费多少有点偏科，你端水端得十分稳定。问你最爱把钱花在哪里？不好意思，这道题拒绝单选——生活这么丰富，当然要雨露均沾。
cards.interpretation_en: Trying to find one dominant obsession in your spending is surprisingly difficult, because every category gets its fair share. Food, shopping, transport, entertainment, and everyday essentials all make regular appearances, but none gets to take over. While other people’s spending has a clear favorite, yours refuses to pick sides. Asked where you love spending most? Sorry—this question is not multiple choice.
cards.core_categories: 餐饮 / 购物 / 交通 / 娱乐 / 生鲜 / 饮品 / 日用 / 学习等多个消费类别均有稳定支出，且不存在明显占据主导地位的单一类别

cards.name: 数据无法捕获之人
cards.tagline: 账单太薄，看不透你。
cards.tagline_en: NOT ENOUGH DATA. YET.COME BACK WITH MORE.
cards.interpretation: 不是你没有消费人格，只是这份账单还不够了解你。几笔交易很容易被一顿大餐、一次购物或者一张机票带偏，用这么一点线索就急着判断你的消费人格，多少有点草率。于是这一次，本算法决定承认自己的能力边界：你的消费人格暂时成功逃过数据捕获。换一份更完整的账单再来，我一定会看破你的！
cards.interpretation_en: It’s not that you don’t have a spending personality—this bill simply doesn’t know you well enough yet. A handful of transactions can be easily distorted by one dinner, one shopping trip, or one flight, and assigning you a personality from that would be a little too confident. So this time, the algorithm admits defeat: you’ve successfully escaped data capture. Bring back a fuller statement, though, and I have the confidence to understand you better next time!
